rationales: 2.70 g/cm³ is approximately the density of aluminium, not gold.
7.86 g/cm³ is approximately the density of iron, not gold.
Gold has a density of about 19.3 g/cm³.
4.88 g/cm³ is not the density of gold.
Diamond is a crystalline solid with an ordered structure.
Plastic is generally classified as an amorphous solid.
Rubber is generally classified as an amorphous solid.
Glass is an amorphous solid, not a crystalline solid.
KCl solubility changes somewhat with temperature.
KNO₃ solubility increases markedly with temperature.
NaNO₃ solubility increases substantially with temperature.
NaCl solubility changes very little with temperature.
ns² is the general valence configuration of alkaline-earth metals.
ns²np¹ is the general valence configuration of Group 13 elements.
ns²np² is the general valence configuration of Group 14 elements.
Alkali metals have one valence electron, giving them the configuration ns¹.
Water is polar and generally dissolves polar or ionic substances.
Carbon tetrachloride is non-polar and dissolves many non-polar covalent compounds.
NaCl is an ionic compound, not a solvent.
Potassium chloride is an ionic compound, not a solvent.
55.3 mm Hg is far below water's vapour pressure at 100°C.
49.4 mm Hg is far below water's vapour pressure at 100°C.
At 100°C, water's vapour pressure is 760 mm Hg.
355.1 mm Hg is below water's vapour pressure at 100°C.
Increasing external pressure does not generally increase a liquid's equilibrium vapour pressure at a fixed temperature.
Stronger intermolecular forces tend to lower vapour pressure.
Greater molecular polarity often strengthens intermolecular attractions and lowers vapour pressure.
Increasing temperature increases a liquid's vapour pressure.
A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Eight electrons would represent four shared pairs, not a triple bond.
Four electrons represent two shared pairs, as in a double bond.
Three electrons cannot make the three shared pairs of a triple bond.
C₆H₆ contains twelve atoms, so it is not triatomic.
HCl contains only two atoms, so it is diatomic.
H₂O contains three atoms, so it is triatomic.
H₂SO₄ contains seven atoms, so it is not triatomic.
The M shell is the third shell and has less energy than the N shell.
The N shell is the fourth shell and has the highest energy among these options.
The L shell is the second shell and has less energy than the M and N shells.
The K shell is the first shell and has the lowest energy among these options.
C₂H₄ contains a carbon–carbon double bond.
C₂H₂ contains a carbon–carbon triple bond.
CH₄ has single covalent bonds between carbon and hydrogen.
O₂ contains a double covalent bond.
Most metal oxides are basic rather than acidic.
Metals generally react with oxygen to form basic oxides.
Some metal oxides are amphoteric, but this is not the general product.
Carbon dioxide is formed from carbon reacting with oxygen, not from a metal.
18 g is the mass of one mole of water, not one molecule.
18 mg is not the mass of one water molecule or its molar mass.
18 kg is not the molar mass of water.
One water molecule has a mass of about 18 amu; its molar mass is 18 g/mol.
The M shell can hold more than 32 electrons; its maximum is 18.
The M shell has n = 3 and can accommodate 2n² = 18 electrons.
Eight electrons is the maximum for the L shell, not the M shell.
Two electrons is the maximum for the K shell, not the M shell.
Calcium is not the usual material used in flash bulbs.
Aluminium is not the standard metal used in flash bulbs.
Magnesium burns with a brilliant white light and is used in flash bulbs.
Platinum is not used as the flash-producing material in flash bulbs.
